questions.q: In ACID, what does the "A" guarantee?
o: All steps of a transaction succeed together or none take effect
Data stays available on every node even during failures
Concurrent transactions can never see each other's changes
Each transaction is executed on the fastest replica only
questions.w: Atomicity means all-or-nothing. A failure halfway rolls every step back. Availability is a different idea, from CAP.

questions.q: A transfer debits account A, then the server crashes before crediting B. Which ACID property makes the debit disappear after recovery?
o: Atomicity, using the write-ahead log to undo partial work
Isolation, because other transactions never see the debit
Consistency, because balances must always stay positive
Durability, because committed data survives the crash
questions.w: The write-ahead log lets the database undo uncommitted changes on restart. That is atomicity in practice.

o: Once a commit is acknowledged, the data survives a crash
The database can never go down while handling writes
Stored data is always encrypted with a strong cipher
Old versions of every row are kept forever for audit
questions.w: Durability is usually delivered by flushing the write-ahead log to disk before acknowledging the commit.

questions.q: Which isolation problem occurs when a transaction reads a row twice and gets different values because another transaction committed in between?
o: Non-repeatable read: the same row returns a different value
Dirty read: the transaction sees uncommitted changes
Phantom read: new rows appear in a repeated range query
Lost update: two writers silently overwrite each other
questions.w: A dirty read sees uncommitted data. A non-repeatable read sees two different committed values of the same row. A phantom read sees new or missing rows in a repeated range query.

questions.q: What does BASE stand for in the context of distributed data stores?
o: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventual consistency
Balanced, Atomic, Serializable, Efficient replication
Backup, Archive, Snapshot and Export for every node
Basic Atomic Storage Engine with strict consistency
questions.w: BASE trades strict consistency for availability and scale: the system keeps answering and replicas converge over time.

questions.q: Which system is the better fit for an account ledger where a balance must never be wrong, even briefly?
o: A relational database with ACID transactions
An eventually consistent key-value store
A cache in front of the database with a long TTL
A full-text search index fed by change events
questions.w: Money needs strong consistency and atomic multi-row updates. Eventual consistency suits feeds, counters and caches.

questions.q: A shopping-style social feed shows a like count that is a few seconds stale on some replicas. Which description fits?
o: Eventual consistency, an accepted BASE trade-off
A violation of atomicity inside one transaction
A durability failure after a database crash
A deadlock between two competing transactions
questions.w: Replicas that lag but converge are eventually consistent. For a like count that trade-off buys availability and speed.

questions.q: Which statement about ACID versus BASE is correct?
o: They are ends of a spectrum, and systems often pick per operation
BASE databases are unable to commit data at all
ACID databases can never be run across several nodes
BASE guarantees stronger consistency than ACID does
questions.w: Real systems mix them: for example strong consistency for payments and eventual consistency for analytics in the same product.
